transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I guess what finally made me make an appointment is that I've been making these, well, really small but kind of embarrassing mistakes lately. 

It's probably not a huge deal, but I keep turning in applications or, like, my research notes, and I'll realize later I mislabeled an artwork date or accidentally skipped a question entirely. And the thing is, I honestly thought I had checked everything perfectly before handing it in. I just feel awful about it. Is that... does that make sense as a reason to be here?
Looking back at your childhood and school years, did you experience similar difficulties with attention or making careless mistakes?

Um, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I was a pretty good kid overall, I think. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it actually was. 

But, um... yeah, back in elementary school, my teachers were always really nice and they would write that I had good ideas. It's just that I... well, I kind of had a habit of forgetting to turn in my worksheets. Or I'd somehow lose the instructions for assignments. I'd just miss these little details, you know? It wasn't on purpose or anything. My parents actually had to check my backpack every single night just to make sure things didn't get lost. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm answering your question right. I know a lot of kids are probably a little disorganized, so I don't know if that's helpful or not.
{"intent": "Screen for core depressive symptoms to differentiate F32.9 from F90.0 and F41.1", "question": "Outside of feeling bad about these mistakes

Um, outside of feeling bad about the mistakes? Well... I mean, I think I'm mostly okay? I don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much. 

I guess... I don't really feel sad or down most of the time, if that's what you mean. I mean, sure, I get a little frustrated with myself when I mess up, but I think I'm generally a pretty positive person. I still enjoy doing things, like my research and looking at art, and hanging out with friends. I don't feel hopeless or anything like that. 

I just... I just want to do a good job and not keep making these silly errors. Does that make sense? I hope that's what you were asking. I'm really trying to give you the right information.
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about a variety of different things in your daily life, and having a hard time controlling that worry?

Um, constantly worrying? I... I don't think so. I mean, I definitely don't want to come across as some kind of nervous wreck. 

I guess I worry a little bit about my classes and making sure I'm doing things right, especially with all those little mistakes I mentioned. But it's not like I'm worrying about everything all the time. I think I can usually manage it okay once I realize I'm getting stressed. It doesn't feel out of control or anything like that. 

I really try to just stay focused on doing my best. Is it okay that I don't feel super anxious all the time? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
